recs.x:
As you will see if you play with my Georgia simulator, when you have a situation where Benford's law does not apply even a small change in voter turnout or in a candidate's share can cause large changes in the first digit distribution. Because of this, and the large number of cities and counties we have in the US where the underlying population does not follow Benford, there is essentially a large randomness in the first digit distributions.
